propositions: Ticket directory creation via os.makedirs happens outside the write lock before the first event file is written, creating a vulnerable window where process interruption leaves an empty directory that fsck reports as MISSING_CREATE or FOREIGN_STORE_PATH.

New staging module creates directory and first event atomically in a dot-prefixed temporary path, then publishes both together via single os.rename under the existing write lock, so interruption leaves only invisible staging debris.
Temp path convention .tmp-newticket-<pid>-<uuid4hex> with leading dot is excluded from fsck checks by existing scanner rules for dot-prefixed entries, requiring no scanner changes.

Stale staging directories from dead processes are cleaned by bounded best-effort sweep on writer start using process start-time stamps to defeat pid recycling, respecting bug 043f by never touching ticket dirs or store data.
Both single-event and batch event write paths share _prepare_event and are converted to use StagedEvent.promote, closing the interruption window for batch creates as well.
Related sites in event_append, inbound_translate, and dispatch_one are converted or explicitly exempted; dot-prefixed lock dirs, marker dirs outside worktree, and pointer writers are out of scope.
